author: Siddhant Adlakha
description: The Cannes competition title and TIFF Special Presentation raises, then quickly drops, intriguing questions about the connection between its director protagonist's colonial-era period piece and personal reckoning with fatherhood.
title: Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s ‘The Beloved’ Stages a Father-Daughter Reckoning That Doesn’t Quite Cohere

author: Olga Samofalova
description: The painter, who has works in public and private collections including the Museum of Contemporary Art, Beijing; Laura Lee Brown and Steve Wilson's 21c Museum in Louisville; and the Rockwell Museum in Corning, New York, spent six years playing bass in a New York rock band, an experience he credits with teaching him discipline. He remains skeptical of his own artistic success, describing a career built more on persistence than any singular breakthrough moment.
title: Tim Kent’s New Show Is About Rest But He Can’t Stop Working

author: Elisa Carollo
description: Now in its second edition, SPLIT LEVEL trades New York's crowded art-week calendar for a slower, salon-style format hosted inside Rimadesio's NoMad showroom. The fair's model was inspired by Cedar's own gallery, Good Naked, which similarly emerged from a need to find sustainable, nontraditional ways to support cultural production.
title: Artist and Dealer Jaqueline Cedar’s SPLIT LEVEL Fair Bets on a More Intimate Art Market Model

author: Mónica Marie Zorrilla
description: Jimmy Pitaro is turning ESPN Unlimited into an NFL streaming hub with NFL Network, fantasy football and a Super Bowl, even without every game.
title: Jimmy Pitaro Built ESPN’s Streaming Future. But How Many Fans Are Paying for It?

author: Elisa Carollo
description: Born José Campos, the artist left El Salvador as a child and grew up undocumented in the U.S.—experiences that shape a practice spanning painting, sculpture and community-based projects. His new Armory Show works trace the history of the Salvadoran colón and the monetary exchanges that connect diasporic communities to the countries they've left behind.
title: Studio Lenca Has Built a Career on the Ambiguity of the Diasporic Experience

author: Paul Jebara
description: Milan’s defining labels are changing hands. Their histories reveal what a new owner can buy, and what has to be learned.
title: The Families That Made Milan a Fashion Capital

author: Nik Kinley
description: Through decades of consistency and candor, Warren Buffett became a rare source of trust in American business. Leadership expert Nik Kinley explores why Buffett’s departure from Berkshire Hathaway represents a broader loss for business and capitalism.
title: Warren Buffett and the Loss of Capitalism’s Character Witness

author: Wana Udobang
description: The celebrated Nigerian-American artist and poet whose work can be found in institutions like the Museum für Moderne Kunst, LUMA Arles and the Rubell Museum sees ecological and colonial histories as inseparable. Their MoMA PS1 courtyard commission, "Among The Flowers I Learned to Love: A Garden of Decreation," is encoded with childhood memories of safety and care, yet holds space for environmental and childhood fracture.
title: Precious Okoyomon On Play and the Garden as a Revolution of Tenderness

author: Emily Zemler
description: Cussac's Monaco restaurant pairs Mediterranean precision with lavish service, from the opening bread trolley to the final pastry cart.
title: At Les Ambassadeurs in Monaco, Christophe Cussac Serves Generosity by the Trolley
